newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops advance slowly on rebel heartland.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops advance slowly on rebel heartland.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops inched their way forward into the heartland of Tamil Tiger rebels after launching a major offensive on Tuesday to open a strategic land route to the northern government-held town of Jaffna.
Troops backed by helicopter gunships, artillery and tanks advanced five km (3.1 miles) into the rebel-held Wanni region, meeting little resistance, a Defence Ministry statement said.
"Enemy transmissions indicated four Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) cadres were killed and a fair number were wounded," the statement said.
It said there were no troop casualties.

Soldiers left their bases in Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, at first light and headed towards the mostly shrub jungle-covered Wanni region further north, military officials in the region said.
A spokesman for the LTTE's international office in London told Reuters details of the offensive had not yet reached them.
But the rebels said earlier they were prepared to face it.
Officials said the military had been preparing for the offensive since initial plans for one early last month were scrapped due to logistical problems.

The main aim of the offensive, code-named "Jaya Sikurui", or "Sure of Victory", was to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya and the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north, military officials in the north said.
Civilians and aid workers in Vavuniya told Reuters the town was rocked by outgoing army artillery fire ahead of the advance.
Last July, government forces advanced further south of Jaffna, moving about 20 km (12 miles) down from the peninsula to Kilinochchi, forcing their way into the rebel heartland.
The current offensive plans to link Kilinochchi with Vavuniya, establishing a military land supply route all the way to Jaffna.
LTTE rebels are fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict, but the LTTE says the toll is higher.
Military officials in the north said a large number of troops had begun moving out from three places and were most likely heading towards Mankulam, about 40 km (25 miles) north of Vavuniya.
"Air force planes have been taking on known rebel targets in the Wanni region since Monday to soften up the ground for foot soldiers on Tuesday," one military official said.
Aid workers said they were monitoring civilian movements as the offensive was likely to send more people rushing to Wanni's already crowded refugee camps.
About half of the Wanni's 600,000 population were already displaced and living as refugees, a Western aid worker said.
This is the year's second major offensive by government forces. In February they captured another key land route linking Vavuniya with the town of Mannar in the island's west coast.
The rebels did not offer much resistance to advancing troops during that offensive, which lasted 17 days.
